source.title: KairoSphere architecture and runtime audit — prioritized repair plan
source.body:
## Objective
Perform a repository-wide architecture and runtime audit of KairoSphere and deliver an evidence-backed, prioritized repair plan. Do not begin broad refactoring before the audit findings are recorded.

## Known baseline (verify against current HEAD)
- Vite build tool and development server.
- Native JavaScript ES modules; no React/Vue/Angular dependency was present in the previously inspected root package.json.
- Supabase client dependency and Supabase project files.
- Vite config previously set the production base path to `/laughing-waffle/` and development base to `/`.
- Local browser previously failed to render the app at localhost:5173; root cause was not established.
- Prior repository inspection did not include a live local process, browser console, network trace, or full test/build execution.

## Audit workstreams (priority order)

### P0 — Runtime boot and reproducibility
- Inspect current branch/commit, package.json, lockfile, Node engine, Vite config, HTML entry, source entrypoints, and scripts.
- Reproduce startup using the documented Node version and a clean dependency install where possible.
- Check port 5173 occupancy, Vite host binding, strictPort behavior, process exit/logs, and whether Vite silently falls back to another port.
- Verify both localhost and 127.0.0.1 responses, HTML entry, module loading, asset paths, and browser console/runtime exceptions.
- Determine whether the observed browser frame error is caused by server absence, wrong port/host, startup failure, or application runtime failure. Attach exact evidence.

### P1 — Frontend architecture and application integrity
- Map the actual application boot sequence, modules, routing/navigation, state ownership, UI composition, and dependency graph.
- Identify dead, duplicated, conflicting, stale, or unreachable files and scripts.
- Verify responsive behavior and core dashboard/navigation flows.
- Check error boundaries/fallback behavior, loading/empty/error states, and console warnings.
- Distinguish deliberate architecture from accidental complexity; recommend simplification only where supported by evidence.

### P1 — Supabase and security
- Trace client initialization and environment-variable usage; verify no secrets are committed or exposed.
- Inspect auth/session restoration, sign-in/sign-out, protected access, and failure handling.
- Review database schema/migrations, CRUD paths, validation, and Row Level Security policies against actual client queries.
- Check anonymous/public access, ownership constraints, and data isolation. Do not weaken RLS to make the UI work.
- Verify missing/malformed environment configuration fails safely and is documented.

### P1 — Build and deployment
- Run automated tests and production build; record exact commands, exit codes, and relevant output.
- Validate GitHub Pages base path, asset URLs, SPA refresh/navigation behavior, and deployment workflow consistency.
- Compare local development and production preview behavior.

### P2 — Quality, maintainability, and performance
- Check accessibility basics, mobile layout, semantic structure, bundle size, unnecessary dependencies, and avoidable runtime work.
- Assess logging/diagnostics and add only high-value observability recommendations.
- Identify obsolete patterns and unused data/code; propose cleanup separately from necessary repairs.

## Required deliverables
1. Architecture map: entrypoints, major modules, data flow, external services, build/deploy path.
2. Runtime diagnosis: reproducible steps, root cause(s), logs/network/browser evidence. Mark anything not testable in the available environment as NOT VERIFIED.
3. Findings register with severity (P0/P1/P2), affected file/line, impact, evidence, and recommended fix.
4. Prioritized repair plan: smallest safe repair first, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and rollback considerations.
5. Test matrix: startup, both loopback URLs, browser render, auth/session, CRUD/RLS, tests, production build, deployed base path.
6. Explicit list of proposed removals/refactors and why they are safe; do not delete or migrate data during the audit.

## Execution constraints
- Audit first; do not make broad architecture changes or destructive cleanup as part of diagnosis.
- Preserve user data and secrets. Never print secret values.
- Do not change repository ownership/access, security settings, billing, or deployment/publication settings.
- If repair is straightforward and non-destructive, propose the exact patch and test it on a separate branch or local working tree; do not merge or deploy.
- Do not claim a test passed unless it was actually run. Separate VERIFIED, FAILED, and NOT VERIFIED.
- If local terminal/browser access is unavailable, complete the static repository audit and provide exact commands for the local operator to run.

## Final report format
- Executive status (Healthy / Degraded / Blocked)
- Confirmed root causes
- P0/P1/P2 findings table
- Architecture map
- Prioritized repair sequence with acceptance tests
- Commands/tests run and results
- Remaining blockers and owner/action needed

comments.text:
## Confirmed page-binding scope (user approved)

Bind navigation, modules, and data contracts together, but only expose implemented destinations.

### Current evidence
- `main` currently has a single HTML entry page (`index.html`) and one application entry (`src/app.js`). No multi-page router or page navigation is present in the inspected source.
- The `integration/unified-guided-experience` branch contains `docs/UNIFIED_GUIDED_EXPERIENCE.md`, which defines the intended unified route contract. It is an implementation brief, not proof that those routes currently work.
- That route contract explicitly requires source inspection of the local Readonly Agent before integration. If that source is unavailable, stop rather than fabricate or mock it.

### Target route registry
| Route | Intended page/module | Data binding | Status rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Operations overview | Authenticated opportunity summary | Implement using verified opportunity data |
| `/assistant` | Unified assistant / Readonly Agent | Verified read-only adapter only | Block until actual agent source/API is inspected |
| `/opportunities` | Opportunity pipeline and intake | `opportunities` table via existing adapter and RLS | Existing capability; map and test |
| `/opportunities/:id` | Opportunity detail | One owner-authorized opportunity plus related records | Expose only if real detail/data contract exists |
| `/operations` | Operational module index | Registry of implemented modules | Hide/defer modules without real destinations |
| `/inventory` | Inventory | No verified inventory contract yet | Do not expose as functional |
| `/tasks` | Durable tasks | No verified task contract yet | Do not expose as functional |
| `/approvals` | Approval queue | No verified approval contract yet | Do not expose as functional |
| `/activity` | Verified activity/audit | No verified activity contract yet | Do not expose as functional |

### Required binding rules
1. One route registry is the source of truth for navigation, active states, direct URL loads, refresh, back/forward, and unknown routes.
2. Each route resolves to an explicit page module; no dead links or unrelated fallback rendering.
3. Each page declares its data adapter and permission requirement. Supabase Auth remains the single identity provider; existing opportunity RLS remains authoritative.
4. Keep USD/SRD distinct and distinguish verified, user-entered, inferred, estimated, and missing data.
5. Add route tests and page/data-contract tests. Verify signed-out, expired-session, loading, empty, error, and mobile states.
6. Do not add placeholder routes as if they are operational. Do not weaken RLS, add a second auth system, or fabricate the Readonly Agent integration.
7. Implement on a dedicated integration branch/PR only after the current branch/PR landscape and local agent source are reconciled. Do not merge, deploy, or apply migrations as part of this work.

Deliver a route-to-module-to-data matrix with exact file paths and evidence, then implement the smallest verified slice.

comments.text:
## Additional approved architecture requirement — supplier-to-procurement workflow

During the architecture audit, route/module/data-binding work, and subsequent modifications, locate and inspect the existing complementary file or documentation that defines the complete supplier-to-procurement workflow. Do not create a parallel workflow or assume its location/content.

Trace and map every existing implementation and link into that workflow, including navigation/routes, page modules, shared domain models, data adapters/tables, supplier records and qualification, sourcing/RFQ, quotation comparison and award, requisition, purchase order, approval, delivery/receiving and inspection, invoice matching, payment status, and audit/activity history wherever those stages are supported by the actual repository and data contracts.

Deliver:
- Exact file path(s), branch/ref, and current implementation status for the complementary workflow material.
- A supplier-to-procurement lifecycle map showing each stage, route/page/module, data source, transition, permission/approval gate, and downstream link.
- A gap/dependency report identifying existing reusable links, broken or missing links, duplicate logic, unsupported stages, and obsolete structures.
- A phased integration plan that binds only verified modules and real data contracts; explicitly mark proposed or unavailable stages as NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT VERIFIED.

Treat the workflow document as a reference contract to reconcile with the live code, not as proof that a feature exists. Preserve the established Vite + vanilla JS + Supabase architecture unless evidence justifies a change. No fabricated records, placeholder modules presented as functional, schema migrations, destructive cleanup, merge, or deployment without the applicable review and approval.

comments.author: KairoSphere144
comments.text:
## Repository reconciliation completed — supplier/procurement

Inspected all 14 repository branches and the full recursive tree of `feature/warehouse-operations-foundation`. The relevant existing foundation is organization membership, products, warehouses, append-only `stock_movements`, and ledger-derived `inventory_balances`, with adapters in `src/inventory.js` and UI in `index.html` / `src/app.js`.

The warehouse branch README explicitly lists suppliers, purchase requests, purchase orders, and receiving as planned next work. No supplier master, RFQ, quotation, requisition, PO, approval, receipt inspection, invoice matching, or payment-status implementation was found. Generic stock receipt is not equivalent to procurement receiving.

Searched the user's Library for companion material. Located `Physical_to_Digital_Inventory_System.xlsx`, `StockFlow_Concept_Brief.pdf`, and `StockFlow_Lead_Tracker.xlsx`; these are supporting inventory/sourcing materials, not a complete end-to-end procurement specification. No live business data was used.

Created branch `integration/supplier-procurement-workflow` from `feature/warehouse-operations-foundation` and opened draft PR #19: https://github.com/KairoSphere144/laughing-waffle/pull/19

PR #19 adds `docs/SUPPLIER_TO_PROCUREMENT_WORKFLOW.md` and links it from README. It defines lifecycle stages, source-of-truth relationships, approvals, RLS, three-way matching, currency rules, and the required integration from accepted goods receipts into the existing append-only stock ledger. All procurement stages are explicitly marked NOT IMPLEMENTED until code exists.

This is a documentation/integration-contract change only. No procurement application code, migration, or live database change has been made. No tests/build were run. Next coding increments are supplier master/qualification, RFQ/quotes, requisition/award, PO, receiving/inspection-to-stock, invoice matching/payment evidence, then supplier performance and end-to-end tests.
